Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone and wait for further instructions. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s Q2 results. With me on the call are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team, including David Patel, our Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands delivered a solid Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

In today's discussion, we'll touch on our overall financial performance, including the decomposition of our organic sales growth; the factors driving our gross margin expansion; our geographic results across developed and emerging markets; and our outlook for the rest of the year, including organic sales guidance. These areas highlight the underlying momentum in our business across our portfolio of snacks, beverages, personal care, and household essentials.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Mark. As Mark mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.25 billion, representing a 6% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis and 4.5% on an organic basis. Gross margin expanded 150 basis points year-over-year to 42.8%, our strongest quarterly result in over two years, driven by effective management of commodity costs, strategic pricing, and favorable mix shifts. Operating income rose to $685 million, up 12% from last year, while diluted earnings per share came in at $1.28, exceeding our expectations. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start by breaking down our Q2 organic sales growth, which clocked in at a strong 4.5% globally—our best quarterly result in more than two years and ahead of our initial expectations. Organic growth is our key metric here at GCB, giving a clean view of our 25 iconic brands by excluding currency swings, acquisitions, and divestitures. It boils down to three core components: volume, price, and mix, providing transparency into demand strength, pricing power, and portfolio health.

On volume, we achieved +2.1% growth, marking solid market share gains across 70% of our tracked categories according to Nielsen and IRI data. This was up 210 basis points from the prior year, supported by distribution gains and innovation. In North America, which is 45% of our sales, volume rose 3.4%, led by household care where our latest enzyme-enhanced laundry pods drove 12% category share through proven stain-fighting performance. E-commerce on platforms like Amazon and Walmart grew 18%, pulling share from private labels as retail traffic softened. Europe, at 35% of sales, saw +1.2% volume despite a 1% category decline in key markets like Germany and the UK; our premium gel laundry balls expanded distribution 8% in modern trade channels, countering plastic eco-taxes. Emerging markets contributed +1.8%, with Latin America at +4.5% from precision grooming razors gaining 15% in Brazil and Mexico, and Asia up +0.9% via sachet packs boosting rural reach for our hair care lines by 22% in India, despite some lockdown aftereffects in China.

Our Velocity 2025 program, with $500 million committed to shopper marketing and micro-distribution, added about 150 basis points to this volume lift, with 65% coming from higher household penetration in fast-growing SKUs.

Turning to price realization, we netted +1.8%, reflecting disciplined list-price increases of 4-6% on 70% of our portfolio earlier this year, offset partially by trade investments. Elasticity stayed within our -0.4x target, meaning minimal volume pushback—far better than promotional-heavy competitors. Health care pricing led at +2.8%, covering menthol fluctuations in items like vapor rubs, while beauty held at +1.2% to preserve velocity in premium lines. North America was strongest at +2.4%, Europe +1.5% under price transparency rules, and emerging markets +0.9% via value packs. This has recovered 85% of cost inflation since 2021.

Mix provided the +0.9% tailwind, accelerating premiumization to 25% of sales from 18% two years ago, with these SKUs carrying twice the margins of economy tiers. Beauty and grooming drove 30% of the growth via luxury facials up 25% in Asia and heated razors boosting average selling prices 35% in North America. Home care added +1.6% from professional refills amid office reopenings, and emerging markets surged +2.4% with masstige products like supreme dandruff shampoos. We're pruning low performers to fuel these stars under our Elevate Portfolio strategy.

This balanced decomposition—demand-led volume, margin-restoring price, and profitability-boosting mix—shows a healthy core business outperforming peers like P&G and Reckitt.

Now, let's unpack the drivers behind our gross margin expansion to 42.8%, up 150 basis points and beating our guidance range. This came from three levers: commodities, pricing, and mix, where we executed with precision despite headwinds.

Commodities make up 55% of COGS across snacks, beverages, and household items. Input inflation persisted, but hedging and sourcing kept the overall basket to +4% year-over-year, down from 7% last quarter. Cocoa jumped 28% on West African crop issues, hiking chocolate snack costs 12% sequentially—similar to challenges at Hershey and Mondelez. Palm oil rose 15% from El Niño shortages in Indonesia and Malaysia, key for spreads and personal care, while PET for drinks climbed 8% on North American supply tightness. Yet, our hedging covered 70% of 2024 exposure, fixing 80% of sugar at 10% below spot for drinks and candies. Our AI-powered ERP dashboard with SAP Ariba enabled a 15% shift to Latin American RSPO palm oil, cutting costs 2-3%. North America faced +6% inflation from freight after port issues, EMEA gained 2% on softer energy packaging, and emerging markets like Brazil and India were flat with local corn for chips. Net, a 50 basis point drag this quarter, but we expect breakeven in Q3 as hedges mature and volumes rise.

Pricing delivered over half the expansion—220 basis points—with average increases of 5.2% and elasticity at -2.1x, better than the IRI category average of -2.5x. Premium plant-based bars saw 8-10% hikes with 1.2 points share gain versus high-single-digit category growth. Value cleaners got 3% to hold discounter share at Aldi and Walmart. We gained 0.8 points ACV in oral care by sticking to list prices against Colgate's softer stance. APAC realized +6.5% via Tmall e-com, Europe +4% emphasizing pack transparency in laundry amid shrinkflation scrutiny. Our Kantar-data dynamic pricing added 30 basis points through segmentation, with 4-5% carryover expected.

Mix added 80 basis points via premium shifts: keto snacks and RTD coffee pods grew 18%, now 22% of sales at 10-12 margin points above mass chips. We cut low-margin water 5% as a mix %. North America improved 120 basis points on health & wellness up 25%, EMEA 60 basis points on premium household, emerging 4 points on fortified cereals. Our Margin Maximizer tool against IRI data ensures 95% of launches hit 45%+ margins, pruning 10% of 500+ SKUs yearly for Power Brands focus.

Altogether, this positions us 20 basis points ahead of our 42% long-term target, with 75-125 basis points upside in Q3 barring shocks.

Shifting to geographic performance, our $3.25 billion in net sales grew 6% reported, 4.5% organic. Developed markets were 58% of revenue at $1.89 billion, up 3% organic—steady in a tough backdrop. North America (32% of total) rose 4%, gaining 110 basis points share per Nielsen IRI on power brands like laundry detergents and clean-label skincare; premium lines grew 12% volume despite 5-7% input inflation. Europe (18%) was +1%, with hygiene up 6% on post-pandemic habits, though UK/Euro FX weighed. Margins here expanded 80 basis points to 22.5% via NovaSupply 2.0 AI routing cutting logistics 15%; e-com hit 18% of sales from 12%.

Emerging markets, 42% at $1.36 billion, surged 16% organic (19% constant currency)—our top performance in years, driven by middle-class growth, urbanization, and branded demand. Asia-Pacific (22%) hit 18%, India +22% with 15% volume in snacks/personal care via JioMart/Flipkart D2C, gaining 2.2 ACV points per Kantar; China +9% on functional waters via Tmall despite regs. Latin America (12%) +14%, Brazil +17% in home care hedging Argentina's hyperinflation (FX drag just 2 points). Sub-Saharan Africa +8% on RTD teas out-of-home recovery. Value-premium like bio-detergents hit 8% penetration. Inflation averaged 12% vs. 6% developed, but local production at 85% cut duties/times 25%; Precision Pricing AI held affordability. Margins dipped 50 basis points to 28.2% but countered.

We're committing $500 million extra FY24 capex to emerging hubs like India/Indonesia for greenfield sustainable plants. Developed focus: loyalty apps with 45 million members, at-home personalization. Outlook: developed 2-4% organic FY24, emerging 15-18%, group 8-10% potential, 2-3 point FX risk.

Finally, on outlook: For Q3, organic sales growth of 3% to 5%, stepping up from Q2's 2.7%. This tracks to FY24 organic of 4% to 6%, midpoint 150 basis points above May guide. Risks like FX or consumer slowdowns, but tailwinds from sustainability (30% recycled PET boosting loyalty 10%), AI supply chain (<2% stockouts), and outperformance vs. peers position us strongly. For Q4/FY24 organic guide 4-6%, volume +1.5-2.5%, price/mix +2.5-3.5%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Mark Reynolds:
Thanks, John. Inflation has been a persistent challenge, but our consumers have shown remarkable resilience, particularly in essentials like snacks, beverages, and household care. In developed markets, we've seen some trading down in non-essentials, but our power brands maintained velocity through EDLP positioning and loyalty programs. Volume held up because of trusted efficacy—think superior cleaning or hydration. In emerging markets, rising incomes offset inflation, fueling masstige demand. Elasticity at -2.1x confirms pricing power without major volume erosion. We're monitoring U.S. slowdown risks closely but diversified across categories and regions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan.

Emily Johnson:
Regarding your new product, NutriCrunch keto-friendly snacks, what are the projections for its market impact?

David Patel:
Hi Emily. NutriCrunch has been a breakout star in our premiumization push, launching in Q1 and already at 22% of snack sales contribution. Projections show 25% YoY growth in Q3, capturing 1.5 points share in health & wellness per IRI, outpacing high-single-digit category. E-com and club channels drive 40% of uptake, with 10-12 margin points above core. We'll expand to 20 new SKUs by year-end, targeting $200 million run-rate, leveraging sustainability claims like 30% plant-based ingredients to build loyalty.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Lisa Chen:
Sure, Mike. Promo spend was disciplined at 22% of sales, flat YoY as a percent but optimized for ROI. We focused depth on high-velocity categories, normalizing trade to support +1.8% price realization. In North America, we ramped shopper marketing under Velocity 2025, adding 150 bps volume without excess discounting. Europe complied with regs via transparent promotions, while emerging used micro-segmentation for value packs. Our trade spend platform's Margin Maximizer simulated scenarios against scanner data, ensuring 95% efficiency. Expect similar levels in Q3, protecting RGM while funding innovation.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mark Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q2 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

Geographic performance: developed vs. emerging markets
Decomposition of organic sales growth: volume, price, mix

aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed (58% sales): +3% organic (North America +4%, Europe +1%); emerging (42%): +16% organic (+19% CC; Asia-Pacific +18%, Latin America +14%). FY24 outlook: developed 2-4%, emerging 15-18%.
